properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 8 at 1:07AM CST until November 9 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous
rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Statement, from noon CST today
through late tonight. For the High Rip Current Risk, from noon
CST today through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow
beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could
be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may
experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also
occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State
Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park. Rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide at
452 PM this afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 8 at 12:34AM CST until November 9 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south Texas, including the following areas,
Aransas Islands, Bee, Coastal Aransas, Coastal Kleberg, Coastal
Nueces, Coastal Refugio, Coastal San Patricio, Duval, Goliad,
Inland Kleberg, Inland Nueces, Inland Refugio, Inland San Patricio,
Jim Wells, Kleberg Islands, La Salle, Live Oak, McMullen, Nueces
Islands and Webb.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread forecast rainfall amounts of 2-5 inches will be common
across South Texas. Isolated amounts of 7 to 9 inches remains a
possibility, especially in the vicinity of training and slow
moving storms. While soils will be able to absorb most of this
moisture, the higher rainfall rates, slow storm motion, and
training can quickly lead to localized, urban flooding and in
locations with poor drainage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 8 at 12:27AM CST until November 9 at 3:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM CST this
morning through late tonight. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
from noon today to 3 AM CST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 7 at 9:50PM CST until November 9 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of locally heavy rainfall are expected through early
Monday morning.  The first round is most likely between midnight and
mid-morning Sunday, when 2 to 3 inches with locally 4 or more inches
of rain may fall. The second round is expected Sunday night into
early Monday morning, when an additional 1 to 3 inches with locally 4
inches or more possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Deep South Texas, including the following
counties, Brooks, Jim Hogg and Zapata.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and ditches may
become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Potential for heavy rainfall, including two windows where
rainfall rates could reach 2 inches per hour for two hours both
late tonight and early Sunday morning, and again Sunday night
through mid morning Monday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 7 at 9:05PM CST until November 8 at 2:00AM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Bandera County in south central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 200 AM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 905 PM CST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Medina, Bandera, Tarpley and Hill Country State Natural Area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.
